# Copilot instructions

- Treat the wiki as the source of truth for research knowledge. Keep one canonical Markdown page per paper or article, with metadata and typed links in frontmatter. Derive indexes and graphs from the wiki rather than maintaining a separate knowledge store.
- Ground claims in sources; popularity is not evidence. Use deterministic code for schema validation, ID resolution, and deduplication.
- When recommending papers, consider the reader's interests and what each paper adds to the existing wiki, not just citations, awards, or popularity. Honor explicit ranking or sampling requests, and do not assume the reader has read every wiki entry.
- Keep schemas, workflow skills, task prompts, and harness orchestration separate.
- For paper questions, check the wiki and matching local extract in `sources/` before re-fetching; consult the original when the extract is insufficient. Append a concise, sourced H3 Q&A to the **FAQ** unless already covered. Leave the rest of the page unchanged and validate.
- Apply and verify accepted paper-specific corrections in the canonical wiki page. Use recurring, generalizable feedback to improve future workflows rather than turning a one-off correction into a general rule. When feedback identifies a concrete wiki improvement or helps establish a recurring workflow gap, retain a concise, non-sensitive summary in a relevant GitHub issue or pull request. Link the affected page or workflow and note the expected improvement; reuse existing records rather than duplicating them. Keep raw comments and evaluation notes out of wiki and skill files.
